claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a 17-year-old son named Alex who lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 17, a key factor for eligibility is whether he's in approved education or training. **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (This could include things like A-levels, T-levels, NVQ Level 3 or below, or other approved courses.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 17 and not currently in education or training, there may still be a possibility for Child Benefit to continue for a limited time.

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** (If he has, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with the careers service or anything like that. He just finished school and is at home at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have a clear picture of your situation.

Let me also confirm one more thing: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.text:
## Eligibility Assessment for Alex

I'm afraid based on the information you've provided, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

Since Alex is 17 years old, Child Benefit can only continue if certain conditions are met:

1. **If he's in approved education or training** - Child Benefit continues for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. However, Alex is not currently in education or training.

2. **20-week extension option** - Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, Alex has not registered with either of these.

Since neither of these conditions applies to Alex's situation, Child Benefit eligibility has ended.

**What could change this:**
- If Alex enrolls in approved education or training (such as A-levels, T-levels, or NVQ Level 3 or below), you could claim Child Benefit again
- If Alex registers with a careers service soon after leaving education, you may be able to claim for up to 20 weeks

If Alex's circumstances change, you can make a new claim at that time.
